name: Slow Cooker Beef Cheeks in Red Wine Sauce
evidence: Closest catalog neighbour is 'Beef Bourguignon Bowls' (beef-chuck-roast, bacon, mushrooms, beef-broth, over starch) - same beef + slow-braise but a genuinely different plate: distinct cut (beef cheeks, which the catalog has zero of), no bacon/mushroom bourguignon garniture, red-wine-forward sauce (bourguignon entry lists beef broth not wine), and no starch base vs the bowl format. Other beef braises (Classic Beef Stew=potatoes, Greek Stifado=onion/tomato, Irish=Guinness stout, Bo Kho=lemongrass) are unrelated flavor families. Not present in accepted-slugs.json.
borderline_note: Adjacent to beef-bourguignon-bowls on the red-wine-braise axis; kept because cut + garniture + starch-format + no-mushroom/bacon distinguish the dinner. Decider may downgrade if it wants only one French red-wine beef braise in the catalog.
cross_protein_collision: A red-wine slow-braise of pork cheeks or lamb shanks (mirepoix + wine + thyme/bay, no starch) would be structurally the same dish under a different protein - flag for the merge pass if a pork-cheek or lamb-shank red-wine braise appears in another selector's pool.
